text:
Jen: Hey team, seeing repeated 500s from the frontend in prod. Browser console shows x-request-id=req_89a7 and trace_id=4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736. Any quick way to fetch full request logs and spans? Happened ~14:22 UTC.
Mike: If you have the trace id, Console -> Traces is fastest: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736. That view links spans + related logs.
Jen: I don't have console access atm, prefer CLI.
Mike: CLI snippets that help: 
```
# fetch trace JSON
redwoodctl traces get --trace-id 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 --output json
# then search logs by request id
redwoodctl logs query --filter 'request_id:req_89a7' --service api-gateway --since '10m ago'
# correlate logs only from a trace
redwoodctl logs correlate --trace-id 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 --minutes 10
```
Jen: ran the logs query, returned nothing.
Sam: double-check header name — our frontend sometimes rewrites to `x-redwood-request-id`. Also make sure you're hitting the correct region: add `--region us-west-2` if the client is in that region. Time window is the usual culprit.
Mike: If request id doesn't show, try grepping message fields too: 
```
redwoodctl logs query --search 'req_89a7' --since '30m ago' --services 'api-*'
```
Sam: Or use Kibana directly: query `message: "req_89a7" AND service:api-gateway` and widen the timepicker.
infra-bot: [automated] Created trace lookup stub for 4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 -> https://console.redwood.ai/traces/4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736 (expires in 24h).
Lisa: If you post the full request id (or DM me) I can run a cross-service correlation and return the raw log lines. Also check the gateway logs — sometimes 50x are from upstream timeouts.
Jen: Full request id posted in DM to Lisa, thanks.
Mike: FYI we're rolling out a helper `ri find-request` in dev-ex next week that wraps traces->logs correlation (will accept either trace id or request id). Should reduce this dance.
Jen: Perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
